missions.name: Mariner 4
missions.purpose: make the first close-up observations of Mars
missions.finding: a cratered surface that looked more like the Moon than the canals once imagined
missions.challenge: a single fast flyby with a limited number of images and a long-distance data link
missions.legacy: return the first close-up images of another planet

missions.name: Viking 1
missions.purpose: orbit Mars, land safely, and investigate the surface and atmosphere
missions.finding: a rocky plain, a thin atmosphere, and soil chemistry tested by experiments searching for signs of life
missions.challenge: landing safely on an unfamiliar surface while operating science instruments for far longer than the planned primary mission
missions.legacy: make the first successful U.S. landing on Mars and return years of surface measurements

missions.name: Viking 2
missions.purpose: study the Martian surface, atmosphere, and possible signs of life
missions.finding: a broad northern plain, seasonal frost, and soil results that remained difficult to interpret as evidence of life
missions.challenge: working through a cold, dusty environment while sending data across the distance between Mars and Earth
missions.legacy: show that Mars has varied surface conditions and that life-detection results require careful interpretation

missions.name: Mars Pathfinder
missions.purpose: demonstrate an affordable landing system and deploy the Sojourner rover
missions.finding: rocks and soil in a flood-carved region, including evidence that water had shaped the landscape
missions.challenge: surviving entry, descent, and landing with airbags before beginning surface operations
missions.legacy: prove that a small rover and an innovative landing system could explore Mars together

missions.name: Mars Odyssey
missions.purpose: map the planet's elements and minerals and look for evidence of water
missions.finding: hydrogen-rich regions beneath the surface that pointed to widespread water ice
missions.challenge: turning global measurements from orbit into detailed maps useful to later landing missions
missions.legacy: create a long-running communications relay and guide the search for water on Mars

missions.name: Mars Global Surveyor
missions.purpose: map the planet's surface, atmosphere, and magnetic environment
missions.finding: a global topographic picture, signs of ancient water-carved terrain, and localized crustal magnetic fields
missions.challenge: using aerobraking to gradually reshape its orbit while protecting the spacecraft and its instruments
missions.legacy: provide a detailed global baseline that transformed how scientists understood Martian geology

missions.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
missions.purpose: study the planet's climate and geology and scout safe landing sites
missions.finding: high-resolution terrain and mineral evidence showing that liquid water shaped many ancient environments
missions.challenge: balancing detailed science observations with the work of relaying data for surface missions
missions.legacy: help scientists choose landing sites and deliver a vast, detailed archive of Mars observations

missions.name: Phoenix
missions.purpose: dig into northern Martian soil and examine the local water cycle
missions.finding: water ice just beneath the surface and soil chemistry that included perchlorate
missions.challenge: using a robotic arm to dig and deliver samples in a harsh polar environment
missions.legacy: confirm that accessible water ice lies in the Martian arctic soil

missions.name: Curiosity
missions.purpose: assess whether ancient Mars had conditions that could support microbial life
missions.finding: evidence that an ancient lake in Gale Crater had chemistry suitable for microbial life
missions.challenge: landing a large rover with a sky-crane system and navigating a rocky landscape
missions.legacy: show that ancient Mars once offered long-lived habitable environments

missions.name: MAVEN
missions.purpose: investigate how Mars lost much of its atmosphere to space
missions.finding: solar wind and radiation strip gas from the upper atmosphere, with loss rates changing over time
missions.challenge: sampling a variable upper atmosphere while coordinating orbital science and communications
missions.legacy: connect atmospheric escape to the long-term climate history of Mars

missions.name: InSight
missions.purpose: measure marsquakes and probe the planet's internal structure
missions.finding: marsquakes and seismic signals that revealed details about the crust, mantle, and core
missions.challenge: placing sensitive instruments on the ground and keeping solar panels clear enough to power them
missions.legacy: make Mars the first planet beyond Earth whose deep interior was measured with seismology

missions.name: Perseverance
missions.purpose: search for signs of ancient microbial life and collect samples for possible return
missions.finding: igneous and sedimentary rocks in a crater that once held a lake and river delta
missions.challenge: landing in rugged terrain and selecting which rock samples are most valuable to preserve
missions.legacy: assemble the first carefully selected Mars sample collection for a possible future return to Earth

missions.name: Mariner 2
missions.purpose: measure Venus and study the solar environment between Earth and the planet
missions.finding: an intensely hot Venus and a continuous solar wind flowing through interplanetary space
missions.challenge: reaching another planet with early deep-space technology and maintaining a reliable radio link
missions.legacy: complete the first successful mission to another planet

missions.name: Mariner 10
missions.purpose: use a Venus gravity assist to make repeated close observations of Mercury
missions.finding: a heavily cratered surface, a thin atmosphere, and a global magnetic field
missions.challenge: withstanding intense solar heat while revisiting Mercury on a carefully timed orbit
missions.legacy: provide the first close-up view of Mercury and reveal its unexpectedly strong magnetic field

missions.name: Pioneer 10
missions.purpose: make the first close study of Jupiter and test a route through the asteroid belt
missions.finding: Jupiter's cloud bands, large moons, and intense radiation environment
missions.challenge: crossing the asteroid belt and surviving Jupiter's powerful radiation belts
missions.legacy: open the way for spacecraft to travel safely through the outer Solar System

missions.name: Pioneer 11
missions.purpose: use a Jupiter encounter to reach Saturn and examine its rings and magnetic environment
missions.finding: new views of Saturn's rings and measurements of the planet's magnetosphere
missions.challenge: threading a safe path past Saturn while navigating a radiation-rich region
missions.legacy: perform the first close flyby of Saturn and help plan later outer-planet missions

missions.name: Voyager 2
missions.purpose: explore the giant planets and continue outward on a trajectory beyond them
missions.finding: Uranus's unusual magnetic field, dark rings, and previously unseen moons
missions.challenge: making one fast encounter count, with limited chances to aim instruments and transmit observations
missions.legacy: become the only spacecraft to visit Uranus and later Neptune up close

missions.name: Galileo
missions.purpose: study Jupiter's atmosphere, magnetosphere, rings, and large moons
missions.finding: evidence of subsurface oceans at Europa and active volcanism on Io
missions.challenge: operating after its main high-gain antenna failed and returning data through a slower backup link
missions.legacy: reveal a dynamic Jupiter system and strengthen the case for ocean worlds

missions.name: Juno
missions.purpose: map Jupiter's gravity, magnetic field, atmosphere, and interior
missions.finding: deep atmospheric flows, complex polar storms, and clues to Jupiter's core
missions.challenge: flying close to Jupiter's radiation belts while protecting sensitive instruments
missions.legacy: reshape the picture of how Jupiter formed and how its deep atmosphere behaves

missions.name: MESSENGER
missions.purpose: map Mercury and investigate its geology, magnetic field, and volatile materials
missions.finding: water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters and a large iron-rich core
missions.challenge: managing extreme heat and repeated orbital passes close to the Sun
missions.legacy: transform Mercury from a briefly visited world into a mapped planet

missions.name: Magellan
missions.purpose: map the cloud-hidden surface of Venus with synthetic aperture radar
missions.finding: volcanoes, vast lava plains, impact craters, and a surface shaped by geologic activity
missions.challenge: seeing through dense clouds and managing the spacecraft's changing orbit
missions.legacy: map most of Venus in detail for the first time

missions.name: Pioneer Venus Orbiter
missions.purpose: study Venus's atmosphere, ionosphere, and interaction with the solar wind
missions.finding: a complex atmosphere, changing cloud patterns, and a long, comet-like ion tail
missions.challenge: gathering observations through a hot, corrosive planetary environment from orbit
missions.legacy: build a broad picture of Venus's atmosphere over more than a decade

missions.name: New Horizons
missions.purpose: make the first close reconnaissance of Pluto and its large moon Charon
missions.finding: mountains, glaciers, hazes, and a surprisingly active surface on Pluto
missions.challenge: collecting detailed data during one brief flyby after a journey of nearly a decade
missions.legacy: give humanity its first close look at Pluto and open a path to the Kuiper Belt

missions.name: Dawn
missions.purpose: orbit two large bodies in the asteroid belt and study the early Solar System
missions.finding: bright salt deposits and evidence of a past briny environment on Ceres
missions.challenge: using ion propulsion to travel between and orbit two distant worlds
missions.legacy: become the first spacecraft to orbit two extraterrestrial destinations

missions.name: Rosetta
missions.purpose: escort a comet around the Sun and deliver the Philae lander to its surface
missions.finding: a two-lobed comet releasing gas and dust as sunlight warmed its surface
missions.challenge: matching the comet's motion and operating in its weak, changing gravity
missions.legacy: make the first long-term study of a comet from orbit and the first landing on one

missions.name: DART
missions.purpose: test whether a spacecraft impact could measurably change an asteroid moonlet's orbit
missions.finding: the impact shortened Dimorphos's orbital period around Didymos
missions.challenge: autonomously targeting a small moonlet millions of miles away in the final minutes
missions.legacy: demonstrate a tested technique for changing the motion of a near-Earth asteroid

missions.name: Ranger 7
missions.purpose: send close-up images of the lunar surface before the spacecraft reached it
missions.finding: craters and fine surface details that could not be resolved from Earth
missions.challenge: capturing and transmitting images during a one-way approach ending in impact
missions.legacy: return the first successful close-up photographs from a U.S. lunar mission

missions.name: Surveyor 1
missions.purpose: make a soft landing and examine the lunar surface for future crewed missions
missions.finding: a firm but navigable surface and close-up views of lunar soil
missions.challenge: slowing down and landing gently on a world with no atmosphere to cushion the descent
missions.legacy: show that a spacecraft could land safely and work on the Moon

missions.name: Lunar Orbiter 1
missions.purpose: photograph potential landing regions and map the lunar surface from orbit
missions.finding: terrain details that helped identify safe sites for the Apollo landings
missions.challenge: developing and transmitting film images while circling the Moon
missions.legacy: help prepare the way for human exploration by surveying candidate landing sites

missions.name: Clementine
missions.purpose: map the Moon in multiple wavelengths and test compact spacecraft technology
missions.finding: polar regions that radar observations suggested could contain water ice
missions.challenge: operating a compact spacecraft through changing lighting and demanding orbital observations
missions.legacy: produce a new global lunar map and renew interest in polar resources

missions.name: Lunar Prospector
missions.purpose: map lunar composition, gravity, and magnetic fields from a low polar orbit
missions.finding: enhanced hydrogen near the poles and evidence for small magnetic anomalies
missions.challenge: turning measurements from orbit into a global view of a varied surface
missions.legacy: improve knowledge of lunar resources and the Moon's internal structure

missions.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
missions.purpose: map the surface, measure radiation, and investigate potential landing sites
missions.finding: detailed terrain, temperature extremes, and evidence of water-bearing materials near the poles
missions.challenge: combining high-resolution mapping with long-term measurements from orbit
missions.legacy: create a detailed atlas that supports science and future lunar missions

missions.name: GRAIL
missions.purpose: map the Moon's gravity field using two spacecraft flying in formation
missions.finding: a crust shaped by ancient impacts and a thinner, more fractured structure than expected
missions.challenge: measuring tiny changes in the distance between two orbiters as they passed over lunar features
missions.legacy: produce the highest-resolution lunar gravity map of its time

missions.name: LADEE
missions.purpose: study the Moon's thin exosphere and the dust environment near its surface
missions.finding: a very thin lunar exosphere containing gases including neon and argon
missions.challenge: working in a low orbit while avoiding dust and managing limited fuel
missions.legacy: characterize the Moon's tenuous atmosphere before renewed surface activity

missions.name: Hubble Space Telescope
missions.purpose: observe the universe above the blurring effects of Earth's atmosphere
missions.finding: deep-field galaxies, star-forming regions, and precise measurements that helped constrain the universe's expansion
missions.challenge: correcting an early mirror flaw and maintaining stable observations from orbit
missions.legacy: make precision space astronomy a lasting part of modern science

missions.name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
missions.purpose: study high-energy objects and events through their X-ray emissions
missions.finding: hot gas around galaxies, supernova remnants, and X-ray sources near black holes
missions.challenge: focusing X-rays with nested mirrors and operating far above the radiation belts
missions.legacy: reveal energetic processes that visible-light telescopes cannot directly show

missions.name: Spitzer Space Telescope
missions.purpose: observe cool, dusty, and distant objects in infrared light
missions.finding: hidden star formation, distant galaxies, and planets orbiting other stars
missions.challenge: keeping infrared instruments cold as its supply of liquid helium ran out
missions.legacy: extend infrared astronomy and complement observations across the electromagnetic spectrum

missions.name: Kepler Space Telescope
missions.purpose: measure tiny dips in starlight to find planets crossing in front of their stars
missions.finding: thousands of confirmed exoplanets, showing that planets are common in the galaxy
missions.challenge: detecting minute brightness changes across a huge field of stars for years
missions.legacy: change the search for planets beyond our Solar System from a handful of discoveries to a population study

missions.name: TESS
missions.purpose: survey nearby bright stars for transiting planets
missions.finding: a growing collection of nearby exoplanets suited to follow-up observations
missions.challenge: covering most of the sky in sectors while keeping precise watch on stellar brightness
missions.legacy: identify nearby worlds for detailed study by telescopes on the ground and in space

missions.name: James Webb Space Telescope
missions.purpose: observe the early universe, stellar nurseries, and the atmospheres of exoplanets
missions.finding: early galaxies, forming stars, and chemical signatures in distant planetary atmospheres
missions.challenge: unfolding a large sunshield and mirror through a complex sequence after launch
missions.legacy: open a powerful new infrared view of the universe's earliest eras and distant worlds

missions.name: Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope
missions.purpose: survey the sky for gamma rays from the most energetic cosmic sources
missions.finding: pulsars, active galaxies, gamma-ray bursts, and a changing high-energy sky
missions.challenge: distinguishing fleeting cosmic signals from background events across the whole sky
missions.legacy: make gamma-ray astronomy a continuous, all-sky exploration

missions.name: WISE
missions.purpose: scan the entire sky in infrared wavelengths
missions.finding: hundreds of millions of infrared sources, including cool stars and distant galaxies
missions.challenge: keeping its detectors cold enough to survey the faint infrared sky
missions.legacy: create an all-sky infrared catalog used to find and study objects near and far

missions.name: Parker Solar Probe
missions.purpose: sample the solar wind and trace how energy moves through the Sun's outer atmosphere
missions.finding: switchbacks and changing structures in the solar wind close to the Sun
missions.challenge: surviving extreme heat while repeatedly diving close to the Sun behind a protective shield
missions.legacy: make the first direct measurements from within the Sun's outer atmosphere

missions.name: Solar Dynamics Observatory
missions.purpose: continuously observe the Sun's magnetic activity and changing atmosphere
missions.finding: how magnetic fields drive solar flares, eruptions, and waves through the solar atmosphere
missions.challenge: capturing the Sun in many wavelengths at high cadence without interruption
missions.legacy: provide an uninterrupted record that supports space-weather research and forecasting

missions.name: SOHO
missions.purpose: study the Sun's interior, atmosphere, and the solar wind
missions.finding: the structure of the solar corona and thousands of comets passing near the Sun
missions.challenge: maintaining a steady view of the Sun from a distant operating point
missions.legacy: transform solar physics and become one of the most prolific comet-discovering observatories

missions.name: Ulysses
missions.purpose: measure the solar wind and magnetic field far above and below the Sun's equator
missions.finding: a three-dimensional picture of the solar wind and its changes over the solar cycle
missions.challenge: using a Jupiter gravity assist to reach an orbit unlike the planets' nearly flat paths
missions.legacy: provide the first direct measurements of the Sun's polar environment

missions.name: Landsat 1
missions.purpose: repeatedly image Earth's land surfaces to track natural and human-driven change
missions.finding: a consistent, growing record of forests, farms, coastlines, and expanding cities
missions.challenge: turning satellite images into comparable observations collected over many years
missions.legacy: begin the longest continuous space-based record of Earth's changing land

missions.name: Terra
missions.purpose: study how land, oceans, atmosphere, and clouds interact as one Earth system
missions.finding: global patterns in aerosols, clouds, vegetation, and surface temperature
missions.challenge: coordinating multiple instruments to observe connected Earth processes
missions.legacy: help researchers study the planet as an integrated and changing system

missions.name: Aqua
missions.purpose: measure the water cycle across the atmosphere, oceans, and land
missions.finding: global patterns in water vapor, clouds, precipitation, and sea-surface temperature
missions.challenge: collecting consistent measurements across a planet where weather changes by the hour
missions.legacy: improve understanding of the global water cycle and climate

missions.name: OCO-2
missions.purpose: map atmospheric carbon dioxide and identify its major sources and sinks
missions.finding: seasonal changes in carbon dioxide and regional patterns in its distribution
missions.challenge: separating a faint carbon dioxide signal from reflected sunlight and clouds
missions.legacy: provide precise global measurements that help scientists study the carbon cycle
